heading: Louisiana Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Louisiana paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Louisiana income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your pay frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Louisiana's flat income tax system makes salary calculations more straightforward than those in many states. However, withholding deductions, employee benefits and federal payroll taxes still influence the amount deposited into your bank account.

Whether you work in New Orleans, Baton Rouge, Shreveport or Lafayette, understanding your net earnings can help you compare job offers, manage household expenses and make informed financial decisions.

## How to Use the Louisiana Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting your income type.

If you receive a fixed salary, enter your annual earnings before taxes. If you receive hourly wages, enter your hourly rate, regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Choose your payment frequency. Enter the federal and Louisiana income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions and healthcare premiums. Enter withholding amounts that already include any extra tax your employer withheld.

If your earnings are approaching annual federal payroll contribution thresholds, provide your year-to-date taxable wages.

The calculator estimates your individual deductions and displays your remaining take-home income.

For greater accuracy, use your most recent pay stub and withholding certificates.

## How Louisiana State Income Tax Works

Louisiana introduced a flat individual income tax rate of 3% beginning in 2025, replacing its previous progressive rate structure.

Under the flat-rate system, applicable taxable income is generally subject to the same statutory rate regardless of income level.

However, this does not mean every Louisiana employee pays exactly 3% of gross salary.

The applicable deductions and withholding elections can reduce or otherwise affect the amount used to calculate payroll withholding.

For example, an employee earning $70,000 annually should not automatically assume their state income tax is $2,100. That calculation ignores potentially applicable deductions.

A reliable Louisiana salary calculator must account for the official employer withholding methodology rather than simply multiplying gross earnings by the statutory tax rate.

## Understanding Louisiana Form L-4

Louisiana employees generally provide state withholding information using Form R-1300, also known as Form L-4.

This form allows employees to communicate their applicable withholding selections and additional withholding requests to their employers.

Federal Form W-4 serves a separate purpose. Updating federal withholding information does not necessarily update your Louisiana withholding elections.

Review your state withholding certificate when you start a new job, experience a significant change in household income or need to adjust your estimated tax payments.

Employees with more than one job should pay particular attention to whether their combined withholding is sufficient to cover their expected annual tax liability.

Official withholding regulations and updates are available through the [Louisiana Department of Revenue rules and regulations directory](https://revenue.louisiana.gov/tax-policy/rules-regulations/).

## Louisiana Income Tax Calculation Example

Consider a simplified annualized illustration for an employee earning $65,000.

Assume a $12,875 deduction is applicable and there are no other adjustments.

Adjusted annual earnings:

$65,000 − $12,875 = $52,125

Illustrative state tax:

$52,125 × 3% = $1,563.75

Dividing that amount across 26 biweekly pay periods gives approximately $60.14.

This illustrates the relationship between Louisiana's flat tax rate and its withholding deduction. It is not a substitute for the complete official employer formula, which must account for applicable withholding elections and rounding requirements.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Louisiana Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable earnings, payment frequency, filing status and Form W-4 information.

Multiple jobs, eligible credits, other income and additional withholding requests may affect the amount deducted.

Employers follow the calculation methods described in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

For 2026, the annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500.

An employee earning $2,500 in covered wages who has not reached the annual limit would contribute $155.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings.

Unlike Social Security, ordinary Medicare has no standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on Medicare-covered wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

Review the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for additional information.

## Louisiana Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually before taxes and deductions.
Assume the employee receives $2,500 biweekly, all wages are subject to ordinary Social Security and Medicare contributions, and no annual contribution limits have been reached.

Approximately $2,308.75 remains before federal income tax, Louisiana income tax and other deductions.

This is a partial payroll example rather than a complete net paycheck calculation.

Enter your actual withholding amounts and employee benefits into the calculator to estimate your complete take-home earnings.

## Louisiana Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly workers may receive different amounts each payday depending on working hours, overtime, unpaid leave and supplemental compensation.

Suppose an employee earns $28 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$28 × 40 = $1,120

Overtime earnings:

$28 × 1.5 × 6 = $252

Total gross earnings:

$1,372

Assuming all earnings are covered by ordinary federal payroll contributions, Social Security would be approximately $85.06 and Medicare would be approximately $19.89.

Federal and Louisiana income tax withholding would also apply.

Workers in Louisiana's energy, construction, transportation and hospitality industries may receive variable compensation through overtime, shift differentials and bonuses.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about overtime eligibility and exemptions.

## Does New Orleans Have a Local Income Tax?

New Orleans and other Louisiana municipalities generally do not impose a separate personal wage income tax.

Employees therefore generally do not face the municipal payroll income taxes found in certain cities in Ohio, Michigan and Kentucky.

However, local sales taxes, housing expenses, insurance costs and transportation can affect the amount of income available for saving.

These costs should be considered separately from paycheck deductions.

When comparing employment opportunities in different Louisiana communities, calculate your estimated take-home income and then compare expected living expenses.

## Working Offshore or Across State Borders

Louisiana has a substantial energy industry, including employees working offshore or performing duties across multiple jurisdictions.

These employment arrangements can create additional questions about income sourcing, residency and applicable withholding rules.

An employee working in another state may have tax obligations that a Louisiana-only paycheck calculator cannot fully represent.

Similarly, offshore employment can involve specialized federal and state requirements.

Consult your employer's payroll department or a qualified tax professional before applying a standard single-state estimate to complex employment arrangements.

## How Employee Benefits Affect Louisiana Take-Home Pay

Retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other employee benefits can significantly affect your net earnings.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages. Roth contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Qualifying health insurance arrangements may reduce certain taxable wage amounts.

Other deductions are taken after taxes and do not necessarily reduce your taxable earnings.

For accurate results, distinguish between federal income-taxable wages, state income-taxable wages and wages subject to Social Security and Medicare.

An employer offering affordable insurance and generous retirement matching may provide better overall compensation than another employer offering a slightly higher salary.

## Planning Your Louisiana Monthly Budget

Use estimated net earnings rather than gross salary when establishing spending limits.

Include housing, transportation, groceries, utilities, insurance and required debt payments.

Louisiana households may also benefit from maintaining an emergency fund for unexpected property expenses, severe weather disruptions or interruptions in employment.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a suitable savings target, while our [loan payment calculator](/calculators/loan-calculator/) can help evaluate potential borrowing commitments.

If you receive biweekly paychecks, remember that your average monthly income differs from the amount deposited during a typical two-paycheck month.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Louisiana's income tax rate in 2026?

Louisiana applies a flat individual income tax rate of 3%. Actual paycheck withholding depends on applicable deductions, withholding elections and the official employer calculation method.

### Does Louisiana have local employee income taxes?

Louisiana municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes. Federal and state income taxes and applicable payroll contributions still reduce employee earnings.

### Why did my Louisiana paycheck change in 2026?

Louisiana updated its withholding tables effective January 1, 2026. Changes in federal withholding, employee benefits and payroll contribution limits can also affect your take-home pay.
